objects.description: Windows-only alias making uid_t an int. A user identifier type like POSIX uid_t. On non-Windows, the system header provides uid_t, so this definition is not active.
Windows-only alias making gid_t an int. A group identifier type like POSIX gid_t. On non-Windows, the system header provides gid_t, so this definition is not active.
Windows compatibility typedef for ssize_t, mapping to signed __int64 on 64-bit and int on 32-bit. Note: subsequently redefined to SSIZE_T when _MSC_VER is defined (see alias below).
On MSVC, ssize_t is defined as a macro alias to SSIZE_T (from BaseTsd.h). This line effectively makes ssize_t an alias to the Windows SSIZE_T type.

Concrete message container in namespace et that wraps a header byte and a string payload, with an "encrypted" flag and helpers to encrypt/decrypt via a CryptoHandler. Provides serialization format: first byte = encrypted flag (0/1), second byte = header, remaining bytes = payload. HEADER_SIZE is 2. Construction: default empty, from header+payload, from explicit encrypted flag, or from serialized bytes. No ownership beyond its own fields. Unknown details about CryptoHandler are external to this header.

Abstract base class in namespace et that defines the socket I/O and lifecycle interface. Provides pure virtual primitives for hasData/read/write/connect/listen/getEndpointFds/accept/stopListening/close/getActiveSockets, plus concrete helpers for full-buffer reads/writes, protobuf and Packet serialization, and base64 helpers. Intended to be subclassed by platform-specific handlers. Construction is via derived classes; destruction through virtual destructor. Thread-safety and timeout semantics are partially defined by method comments; further details are not present in this header.

TCP socket handler class implementing IPv4/IPv6 operations on top of UnixSocketHandler. Provides non-blocking connect, listen, query of listening file descriptors, and stop-listening. Maintains a map from TCP port to the set of listening socket fds. Details of UnixSocketHandler and SocketEndpoint are external and not defined here.

functions.name: close
functions.description: Windows-only shim that maps POSIX close() to WinSock closesocket(). Defined only when compiling with MSVC; on other platforms the system close() from unistd.h is used. Returns the result from closesocket(). Intended for closing socket descriptors on Windows.
requirements: Available only when _MSC_VER is defined (MSVC build).
fd must be a valid WinSock socket handle obtained from socket/accept/etc.
WinSock must be initialized (e.g., via WSAStartup) before use.
On failure, the return value is SOCKET_ERROR and extended error info is set in WSAGetLastError; callers should handle this accordingly.

functions.name: GetErrno
functions.description: Normalizes/returns the last error code. On Windows, translates selected WinSock errors (WSA*) to their POSIX equivalents; otherwise returns errno. Intended to provide a consistent errno-like value across platforms.
requirements: On Windows, may log fatal for unmapped WSA errors encountered during translation.
Call after a failing system/WinSock call to obtain the last error code.

functions.name: SetErrno
functions.description: Sets the thread-local last error. On Windows, sets the WinSock last error via WSASetLastError; otherwise assigns errno = e.
requirements: Provide a valid error code appropriate for the platform (WinSock WSA* codes on Windows; POSIX errno values elsewhere).

functions.name: et::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& et::operator<<(std::ostream& os, const et::SocketEndpoint& se)
functions.description: Stream insertion operator for et::SocketEndpoint (a protobuf message). Writes the endpoint’s name (if present), followed by ":<port>" if a port is present.
requirements: se should be a valid et::SocketEndpoint; has_name() and has_port() are used to check field presence.
os must be a valid stream; the function appends to its current position.

functions.name: et::split
functions.signature: template <typename Out> void et::split(const std::string& s, char delim, Out result)
functions.description: Splits a string by a single-character delimiter and outputs tokens to an iterator-like output sink (e.g., back_inserter to a container).
requirements: Out must be an output iterator accepting std::string values (e.g., std::back_insert_iterator<std::vector<std::string>>).
No trimming is performed; empty tokens can be produced if delimiters are adjacent or at edges.

functions.name: et::split
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> et::split(const std::string& s, char delim)
functions.description: Convenience overload that splits a string by a single-character delimiter and returns the tokens as a vector of strings.
requirements: No trimming is performed; empty tokens can be produced if delimiters are adjacent or at edges.

functions.name: et::replace
functions.signature: bool et::replace(std::string& str, const std::string& from, const std::string& to)
functions.description: Replaces the first occurrence of substring 'from' in 'str' with 'to'. Returns true if a replacement occurred, false otherwise. Modifies str in place.
requirements: str is modified in place; callers must pass a mutable string reference.
If 'from' is not found, no modification occurs and false is returned.

functions.name: et::replaceAll
functions.signature: int et::replaceAll(std::string& str, const std::string& from, const std::string& to)
functions.description: Replaces all non-overlapping occurrences of substring 'from' in 'str' with 'to'. Returns the number of replacements performed. Modifies str in place.
requirements: If 'from' is empty, no replacements are performed and 0 is returned.
str is modified in place; callers must pass a mutable string reference.

functions.name: et::stringToProto
functions.signature: template <typename T> T et::stringToProto(const std::string& s)
functions.description: Deserializes a protobuf message of type T from its binary string representation using T::ParseFromString. On parse failure, logs a fatal error with a stack trace. Returns the parsed message by value.
requirements: T must be default-constructible and provide bool ParseFromString(const std::string&).
s must contain a valid serialized protobuf for type T; otherwise the process may log fatal and terminate.

functions.name: et::protoToString
functions.signature: template <typename T> std::string et::protoToString(const T& t)
functions.description: Serializes a protobuf message to its binary string representation using t.SerializeToString. On serialization failure, logs a fatal error with a stack trace. Returns the serialized bytes.
requirements: T must provide bool SerializeToString(std::string*).
t must be in a serializable state; otherwise the process may log fatal and terminate.

functions.name: et::waitOnSocketData
functions.description: Blocks up to 1 second waiting for data to become available for reading on the given file descriptor using select(). Returns true if data is available; returns false on timeout or if interrupted by a signal (EINTR). Logs a fatal error for other select() failures.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor (socket or selectable FD) >= 0.
Caller should be prepared for a false return due to timeout or EINTR and may retry.
On certain platforms, select() on non-sockets may be unsupported.

functions.name: et::genRandomAlphaNum
functions.description: Generates a random alphanumeric string of length len using libsodium randombytes_uniform() over [0-61]. Characters include 0-9, A-Z, a-z.
requirements: len must be >= 0; negative values result in invalid behavior when constructing the string.
The function may rely on libsodium’s random number generator; initialization requirements depend on the linked libsodium version (not specified here).

functions.name: et::GetTempDirectory
functions.description: Returns the system temporary directory path as a string. On Windows, uses GetTempPathW and converts to UTF-8; on non-Windows, returns _PATH_TMP.
requirements: On Windows, requires the WinAPI to be available; buffer is sized to 65536 characters.
Returned path may or may not end with a path separator depending on platform behavior; callers should normalize if needed.

functions.name: et::HandleTerminate
functions.description: Installs a custom std::terminate handler that logs uncaught exceptions (with stack trace where available). A simple guard prevents recursive installation within the same thread of execution.
requirements: Should be called once during program initialization to install the handler; repeated concurrent calls are not synchronized.
If an uncaught exception reaches terminate, the handler logs details and the process will terminate.

functions.name: et::InterruptSignalHandler
functions.description: Signal handler intended for interrupts (e.g., SIGINT). Logs a message and exits the process with the signal number as the exit code.
requirements: If used as a POSIX signal handler, it must be registered via signal()/sigaction() by the caller.
The handler calls ::exit(signum), which terminates the process and runs normal cleanup handlers; this may not be async-signal-safe.

functions.name: et::TerminateSignalHandler
functions.description: Signal handler intended for termination signals (e.g., SIGTERM). Logs a message and exits the process with the signal number as the exit code.
requirements: If used as a POSIX signal handler, it must be registered via signal()/sigaction() by the caller.
The handler calls ::exit(signum), which terminates the process and runs normal cleanup handlers; this may not be async-signal-safe.

functions.name: operator==
functions.signature: bool operator==(const google::protobuf::MessageLite& msg_a, const google::protobuf::MessageLite& msg_b)
functions.description: Equality operator for protobuf MessageLite objects. Returns true if both messages have the same type name and their SerializeAsString() outputs compare equal; otherwise false. Note: equality depends on serialized form, which may be affected by non-deterministic field ordering (e.g., map fields) unless deterministic serialization is used.
requirements: msg_a and msg_b must be valid MessageLite objects; SerializeAsString() must be callable on both.

functions.name: operator!=
functions.signature: bool operator!=(const google::protobuf::MessageLite& msg_a, const google::protobuf::MessageLite& msg_b)
functions.description: Inequality operator for protobuf MessageLite objects. Returns true if type names differ or if the serialized bytes via SerializeAsString() differ; otherwise false. See notes on potential non-determinism in serialization for certain field types.
requirements: msg_a and msg_b must be valid MessageLite objects; SerializeAsString() must be callable on both.

functions.name: et::Packet::Packet
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty, decrypted Packet with header initialized to 255 and an empty payload. Useful as a placeholder that can be populated later.

functions.name: et::Packet::Packet
functions.description: Constructs an unencrypted Packet with the given header byte and payload string. Intended for building plaintext packets before optional encryption.
requirements: _header is a byte value (type uint8_t).
_payload may contain arbitrary bytes; its content is not validated.
Resulting packet starts with encrypted flag set to false.

functions.name: et::Packet::Packet
functions.description: Constructs a Packet allowing the caller to explicitly set whether the payload is marked as encrypted. Use when you already know the encryption state of the provided payload.
requirements: _header is a byte value (type uint8_t).
If _encrypted is true, the provided _payload should already be in the encrypted form expected by the CryptoHandler that will be used to decrypt it (inferred from usage).
If _encrypted is false, _payload is treated as plaintext.

functions.name: et::Packet::Packet
functions.description: Deserializes a Packet from its raw wire format: first byte = encrypted flag, second byte = header, remaining bytes = payload. No validation is performed on sizes or values.
requirements: serializedPacket must be at least 2 bytes long; accessing fewer bytes results in undefined behavior.
Byte 0 is interpreted as the encrypted flag (nonzero treated as true).
Byte 1 is the header byte.
Bytes from index 2 to end are taken verbatim as the payload.
If the encrypted flag is true, the payload is expected to be in the encrypted form consumable by the CryptoHandler used later (inferred).

functions.name: et::Packet::decrypt
functions.description: Decrypts the payload using the provided CryptoHandler if the packet is currently marked as encrypted. On success, marks the packet as decrypted and replaces the payload with the plaintext.
requirements: Must only be called when isEncrypted() is true; calling when false triggers a fatal error path (terminates).
cryptoHandler must be a valid, non-null handler compatible with the payload format; it must provide decrypt(string) -> string.
The decrypt operation is expected to succeed for the current payload; errors/exceptions from CryptoHandler are not handled here (inferred).

functions.name: et::Packet::encrypt
functions.description: Encrypts the payload using the provided CryptoHandler and marks the packet as encrypted. The payload is replaced with the ciphertext.
requirements: Must only be called when isEncrypted() is false; calling when true triggers a fatal error path (terminates).
cryptoHandler must be a valid, non-null handler compatible with the payload format; it must provide encrypt(string) -> string.
The encrypt operation is expected to succeed for the current payload; errors/exceptions from CryptoHandler are not handled here (inferred).

functions.name: et::Packet::isEncrypted
functions.description: Returns whether the payload is currently marked as encrypted.

functions.name: et::Packet::getHeader
functions.description: Returns the packet's application-specific header byte.

functions.name: et::Packet::getPayload
functions.description: Returns the stored payload as-is. Note: if isEncrypted() is true, this returns ciphertext; call decrypt() first to obtain plaintext.
requirements: If plaintext is required, callers should ensure the packet is not encrypted (call decrypt() when isEncrypted() is true).

functions.name: et::Packet::length
functions.description: Returns the serialized size in bytes: 2-byte header section plus the current payload length.

functions.name: et::Packet::serialize
functions.description: Serializes the packet into its wire format: byte 0 = encrypted flag (0/1), byte 1 = header, bytes 2..N-1 = payload. Suitable for sending over the network.
requirements: Payload may contain arbitrary bytes and is written verbatim after the two header bytes.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::~SocketHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor allowing derived SocketHandler implementations to clean up platform-specific resources during object destruction. Intended to be invoked automatically when a SocketHandler is deleted through a base pointer.
requirements: Object must be fully constructed before destruction (standard C++ requirement).
Derived classes should ensure any platform-specific resources (e.g., file descriptors, sockets) are released in their destructors.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::hasData
functions.description: Checks whether the kernel reports that the given file descriptor has data available to read. Typically used to avoid blocking reads.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor referencing a readable socket or stream.
Caller should be prepared for either result and handle readiness races (data may change immediately after the check).
Behavior on invalid fd or closed descriptor is implementation-defined/unknown.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::read
functions.signature: virtual ssize_t read(int fd, void* buf, size_t count) = 0;
functions.description: Reads up to count bytes from the file descriptor into the provided buffer. Mirrors POSIX read semantics for sockets.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor that is readable.
buf must be non-null if count > 0 and must have capacity for at least count bytes.
Return value semantics and error reporting follow the implementation; negative return typically indicates error (unknown specifics).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::write
functions.signature: virtual ssize_t write(int fd, const void* buf, size_t count) = 0;
functions.description: Writes up to count bytes from the provided buffer to the file descriptor. Mirrors POSIX write semantics for sockets.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor that is writable.
buf must be non-null if count > 0 and must reference at least count bytes of initialized memory.
Return value semantics and error reporting follow the implementation; negative return typically indicates error (unknown specifics).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::readAll
functions.signature: void readAll(int fd, void* buf, size_t count, bool timeout);
functions.description: Reads exactly count bytes from fd into buf, retrying (e.g., on EAGAIN) until the buffer is filled. May enforce an internal transfer timeout if timeout is true. Throws behavior is not explicitly documented here; see callers for usage.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable descriptor producing at least count bytes.
buf must be non-null and have capacity for at least count bytes.
Function may block until count bytes are read unless an internal timeout is enforced; exact timeout semantics are unknown.
Caller should handle potential exceptions or error handling as implemented elsewhere (unknown from header).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::writeAllOrReturn
functions.signature: int writeAllOrReturn(int fd, const void* buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Attempts to write the entire buffer to fd. Returns the total bytes written on success, or -1 if the operation times out or otherwise fails (e.g., deadlock).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable descriptor.
buf must be non-null if count > 0 and reference at least count bytes of initialized data.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 to detect timeout/failure and avoid assuming partial progress.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::writeAllOrThrow
functions.signature: void writeAllOrThrow(int fd, const void* buf, size_t count, bool timeout);
functions.description: Writes all count bytes to fd, throwing an exception if the operation times out or fails. May enforce an internal transfer timeout when timeout is true.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable descriptor.
buf must be non-null if count > 0 and reference at least count bytes of initialized data.
Caller must be prepared to catch exceptions on timeout/failure; exact exception type(s) are not specified in the header (unknown).
Exact timeout semantics controlled by timeout parameter are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::readProto
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T readProto(int fd, bool timeout);
functions.description: Reads a length-prefixed protobuf message from fd. The function reads a 64-bit length (int64_t), validates it (must be 0..128 MiB), then reads that many bytes and parses into a default-constructed T using T::ParseFromString. Throws std::runtime_error on invalid length or parse failure. If length is 0, returns a default-constructed T.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable descriptor providing data framed as: int64_t length followed by length bytes.
Length must be in the range [0, 134,217,728]; otherwise std::runtime_error is thrown.
T must be default-constructible and provide methods: bool ParseFromString(const std::string&), std::string GetTypeName() (the latter used only in related writeProto logging).
Caller should be prepared to catch std::runtime_error on invalid size or parse failure.
The timeout flag controls whether an internal transfer timeout is enforced during reads; exact semantics are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::writeProto
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
void writeProto(int fd, const T& t, bool timeout);
functions.description: Serializes the protobuf message t to a string, validates the length (0..128 MiB), writes a 64-bit length prefix (int64_t), then writes the payload. Uses writeAllOrThrow, and logs a fatal error (STFATAL) on serialization failure or invalid length.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable descriptor.
T must support bool SerializeToString(std::string*), std::string GetTypeName() and be serializable.
Serialized length must be in the range [0, 134,217,728]; otherwise a fatal log is emitted (process may abort depending on STFATAL behavior).
Caller should be prepared for writeAllOrThrow to throw on timeout/failure.
The timeout flag controls whether an internal transfer timeout is enforced during writes; exact semantics are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::readPacket
functions.description: Reads a length-prefixed binary packet: first reads a 64-bit length (int64_t), validates it (0..128 MiB), then reads that many bytes and constructs a Packet from the data. Returns false when the length is zero (empty message). Throws std::runtime_error on invalid size.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable descriptor providing data framed as: int64_t length followed by length bytes.
packet must be non-null and point to a valid Packet object to receive the result.
Length must be in the range [0, 134,217,728]; lengths outside this range cause std::runtime_error.
Caller must handle a return value of false indicating an empty message.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::writePacket
functions.signature: void writePacket(int fd, const Packet& packet);
functions.description: Serializes packet to a string, validates the length (0..128 MiB), writes a 64-bit length prefix (int64_t), and then writes the serialized bytes using writeAllOrThrow. Logs a fatal error (STFATAL) on invalid message length.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable descriptor.
packet.serialize() must return a string whose size is in [0, 134,217,728]; otherwise a fatal log occurs (process may abort depending on STFATAL behavior).
Caller should be prepared for writeAllOrThrow to throw on write timeout/failure.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::writeB64
functions.signature: void writeB64(int fd, const char* buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Sends a base64-encoded representation of the provided binary buffer over fd. The header declares the API; implementation details (line wrapping, padding, streaming format) are not shown.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, writable descriptor.
buf must be non-null if count > 0 and reference at least count bytes.
Caller should not assume any particular base64 variant or chunking behavior; specifics are unknown from the header.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::readB64
functions.signature: void readB64(int fd, char* buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Reads a fixed amount of base64-encoded data from fd and decodes it into buf. The exact framing and how the fixed amount is determined are not shown in the header.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable descriptor.
buf must be non-null and have capacity for at least count bytes of decoded data.
The exact mapping between encoded byte count and decoded count is not specified; caller should ensure count matches the expected decoded size (unknown details).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::readB64EncodedLength
functions.signature: void readB64EncodedLength(int fd, std::string* out, size_t encodedLength);
functions.description: Reads a base64 string of exactly encodedLength bytes from fd and decodes it into out. Intended for cases where the base64 length is explicitly known/provided.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, readable descriptor.
out must be non-null and point to a valid std::string to receive decoded data.
encodedLength must match the exact number of base64-encoded bytes available on the stream; behavior if mismatched is unspecified (unknown).
No assumption is stated about base64 variant or padding; specifics are unknown.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::connect
functions.description: Opens a connection to the specified endpoint and returns a socket file descriptor, or -1 on failure. The concrete implementation handles transport details.
requirements: endpoint must describe a valid, connectable destination for the implementation (e.g., TCP address/port, domain socket).
Caller must check for a return value of -1 to detect failure.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::listen
functions.description: Starts listening on the provided endpoint and returns the active listening file descriptor(s). May return multiple fds depending on implementation (e.g., IPv4 and IPv6).
requirements: endpoint must describe a valid listening target for the implementation.
Caller should handle zero or more returned fds and manage them appropriately.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::getEndpointFds
functions.description: Returns any file descriptors currently associated with the given endpoint, including listening or other related descriptors.
requirements: endpoint must identify an endpoint known to the implementation.
Returned set may be empty if no fds are associated.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::accept
functions.description: Accepts a pending incoming connection on the listening socket fd and returns a new connection file descriptor. The exact error/timeout behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: fd must be a valid listening socket file descriptor obtained from listen().
Caller must check the return value for failure (e.g., -1) and handle transient errors (unknown specifics).

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::stopListening
functions.description: Stops accepting new connections on the specified endpoint. Typically closes or deregisters listening descriptors associated with the endpoint.
requirements: endpoint must refer to an endpoint previously passed to listen() or known to the implementation.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::close
functions.description: Closes the supplied socket file descriptor and releases associated resources.
requirements: fd must be a file descriptor currently owned by this handler or otherwise safe to close.
After close, fd must not be used by the caller.

functions.name: et::SocketHandler::getActiveSockets
functions.description: Returns a list of all currently active (read/write) socket file descriptors managed by the handler.
requirements: Caller should not assume the returned list remains valid after subsequent operations; snapshot semantics only.
The vector may be empty if no active sockets are present.

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::TcpSocketHandler
functions.description: Constructor for TcpSocketHandler. Initializes a handler that implements IPv4/IPv6 TCP socket operations on top of UnixSocketHandler. Usage: instantiate before calling connect/listen/getEndpointFds/stopListening.
requirements: Object must be constructed before any member function is called.
No explicit construction parameters; any required lower-level initialization is handled internally or by the UnixSocketHandler base class (details unknown).

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::~TcpSocketHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for TcpSocketHandler. Ensures proper cleanup via base class and allows safe polymorphic deletion. Usage: destroy directly or via a base-class pointer to UnixSocketHandler.
requirements: If deleted through a base-class pointer, the destructor will be invoked polymorphically.
Resources associated with the instance will be released according to its implementation (specifics unknown).

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::connect
functions.description: Resolves the hostname/port in endpoint and initiates a non-blocking TCP connection to the server. Built on UnixSocketHandler with additional TCP-specific setup. Usage: provide a valid SocketEndpoint (host/IP and port); check the return value to determine status (exact semantics unknown).
requirements: endpoint must represent a resolvable host/IP and a valid TCP port.
Operation is non-blocking; caller must be prepared to handle asynchronous connection completion or readiness (details of signaling/FD retrieval unknown).
Caller must inspect the returned int for success/failure according to this library’s conventions (exact return contract not documented here).

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::listen
functions.description: Binds and starts listening on all IP addresses for the TCP port indicated by endpoint. Returns the set of listening socket file descriptors. Usage: call with a SocketEndpoint specifying the desired port (and optionally address family); use the returned FDs with event loops or accept logic (details unknown).
requirements: endpoint must specify a valid TCP port. Host/address may be ignored in favor of binding to all interfaces (per description).
Binding to privileged ports may require elevated privileges on some systems.
Caller must handle the returned set<int> appropriately (e.g., store or poll); semantics of empty set indicate failure or no sockets created (exact error reporting unknown).

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::getEndpointFds
functions.description: Returns the listening socket FDs associated with the TCP port described by endpoint. Usage: query after listen to retrieve or re-fetch the active listening FDs for that port.
requirements: endpoint must refer to a port previously passed to listen; otherwise the returned set may be empty (exact behavior unknown).
Caller must handle an empty set as a possible outcome (e.g., not listening or already stopped).

functions.name: et::TcpSocketHandler::stopListening
functions.description: Stops listening on the TCP port described by endpoint and closes all related listening FDs tracked by the handler. Usage: call when the service should cease accepting connections on that port.
requirements: endpoint must refer to a port that the handler is currently listening on; otherwise the call may be a no-op (exact behavior unknown).
After this call, previously returned listening FDs for the port become invalid and must not be used.

import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets the generic string inputs used by the fuzz stubs.
# The stubs consume multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values and a few unsigned ints.
# We provide a single bytes buffer that the fuzzing harness will chunk to
# satisfy each FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) request in order.
#
# Goals:
# - Provide a mix of strings: empty, small ASCII, Unicode-like UTF-8, binary with NULs
#   and length>=2 to satisfy et::Packet(serialized) precondition.
# - Include plausible hostnames and ports embedded in strings for SocketEndpoint-related tests.
# - Include patterns to exercise split/replace/replaceAll logic (delimiters, repeated substrings).
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Encoding format for the output buffer (self-delimiting simple framing):
# [count32][item1_len32][item1_bytes]...[itemN_len32][itemN_bytes]
# Followed by a sequence of 32-bit unsigned ints to satisfy FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) draws.
# Many fuzzing harnesses ignore such framing and just slice; however, since we
# cannot control the harness, we focus on providing a single contiguous buffer
# that contains rich, varied content from which FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
# can extract data consistently. The buffer is constructed to be interesting even
# when read as raw spans.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"a",
    b"0",
    b"test",
    b"hello",
    b"world",
    b"name",
    b"from",
    b"to",
    b"aaaaa",
    b"abcabcabc",
    b"replace_me",
    b"split,values,with,commas",
    b"split::values::with::colons",
    b"leading-",
    b"-trailing",
    b"--adjacent--delims--",
    b"UPPERlower123",
    b"CaseSensitive",
    b"192.168.0.1",
    b"localhost",
    b"example.com",
    b"",
]

UTF8_STRINGS = [
    "προβλήτα".encode("utf-8"),
    "こんにちは".encode("utf-8"),
    "😀😃😄😁".encode("utf-8"),
    "naïve café".encode("utf-8"),
    "ключ".encode("utf-8"),
]

BINARY_CHUNKS = [
    b"\x00\x01\x02\x03",
    b"\xFF\xFE\xFD\xFC",
    b"\x00" * 8,
    b"\x7F\x00A\x00B\x00",  # includes NULs
]

# Some serialized Packet-like buffers (first byte enc flag, second header, rest payload)
# Ensure size>=2
PACKET_LIKE = [
    bytes([0, 0]),
    bytes([1, 0x42]) + b"ciphertext",
    bytes([0, 0xFF]) + b"payload",
    bytes([0, 1]) + b"",  # minimal 2 bytes + empty payload
]

# Strings helpful for replace/replaceAll behavior
REPLACE_PAIRS = [
    (b"aaaa", b"aa", b"b"),
    (b"abcabcabc", b"abc", b"x"),
    (b"nochange", b"zzz", b"y"),
    (b"edge", b"", b"n/a"),  # empty from
    (b"xxx", b"x", b"xx"),   # expansion
    (b"xxxx", b"xx", b"x"),   # contraction
]

# Delimiter bytes to exercise split
DELIMS = [ord(c) for c in [",", ":", " ", "\t", "-", "_", "/", "|", "\x00", "\xFF"]]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    toks = []
    # Base pool
    toks.extend(ASCII_WORDS)
    toks.extend(UTF8_STRINGS)
    toks.extend(BINARY_CHUNKS)
    toks.extend(PACKET_LIKE)

    # Build derived strings
    # Host:port patterns
    hosts = [b"localhost", b"example.com", b"[::1]", b"192.168.1.10"]
    ports = [b"0", b"1", b"22", b"80", b"443", b"65535"]
    for h in hosts:
        for p in ports:
            toks.append(h + b":" + p)

    # Repetition and mixed delimiters
    for d in [b",", b"::", b"--", b"|"]:
        toks.append(d.join([b"a", b"b", b"", b"c"]))
        toks.append(d * 3 + b"middle" + d * 2)

    # Random length >= 2 for Packet(serialized) safety
    for _ in range(6):
        ln = rng.randint(2, 48)
        toks.append(_rand_bytes(rng, ln))

    # Include crafted replace scenarios
    for s, f, t in REPLACE_PAIRS:
        toks.extend([s, f, t])

    # Add strings containing all delimiters
    all_delims = bytes(DELIMS)
    toks.append(all_delims)

    # Ensure variety of small, medium, large
    toks.append(b"A" * 1)
    toks.append(b"B" * 64)
    toks.append(b"C" * 256)

    return toks


def _make_uints(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> list[int]:
    vals = []
    # Bias toward interesting bit patterns and valid port ranges
    interesting = [
        0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256,
        512, 1023, 1024, 2048, 4095, 4096, 65535, 65536,
        0xFFFFFFFF,
    ]
    # Random ports
    for _ in range(10):
        interesting.append(rng.randint(0, 65535))
    # Random general values
    for _ in range(10):
        interesting.append(rng.getrandbits(32))

    # Shuffle and take needed
    rng.shuffle(interesting)
    vals.extend(interesting[:max(count, 32)])

    # Ensure some flags cover combinations for stubs using & masks
    flags = [
        0,
        1, 2, 3,
        4, 8, 12,
        0xAAAAAAAA,
        0x55555555,
        0xFFFFFFFF,
    ]
    vals.extend(flags)

    # More randomness
    for _ in range(max(0, count - len(vals))):
        vals.append(rng.getrandbits(32))

    return vals


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    tokens = _make_tokens(rng)

    # Shuffle tokens but ensure we preserve at least a few guaranteed-length>=2
    rng.shuffle(tokens)

    # Assemble framed section
    out = bytearray()

    # We will build a count-limited list so total size <= MAX_TOTAL.
    # Reserve some space for uints at the end (e.g., 64 uints -> 256 bytes)
    reserve_uint_bytes = 512
    max_payload = MAX_TOTAL - 8 - reserve_uint_bytes  # 8 for count field and some slack

    framed = bytearray()
    count = 0
    for tok in tokens:
        entry = struct.pack('<I', len(tok)) + tok
        if len(framed) + len(entry) > max_payload:
            break
        framed += entry
        count += 1

    out += struct.pack('<I', count)
    out += framed

    # Append a delimiter marker for robustness (optional)
    # Then append a block of unsigned ints for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    uints = _make_uints(rng, 64)
    uint_block = bytearray()
    for v in uints:
        uint_block += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

    # Truncate if needed to keep <= MAX_TOTAL
    remaining = MAX_TOTAL - len(out)
    if len(uint_block) > remaining:
        uint_block = uint_block[:remaining - (remaining % 4)]  # keep aligned

    out += uint_block

    return bytes(out)

import random
from typing import List

# We need to generate a valid protobuf binary for et::SocketEndpoint
# as used by the fuzzer stub. The stub only ever accesses two fields:
# - optional string name
# - optional int32 port (masked to [0, 65535])
# We don't have the exact field numbers, but common patterns for endpoints are:
#   name: field number 1, type string  -> tag = (1 << 3) | 2 = 10
#   port: field number 2, type int32   -> tag = (2 << 3) | 0 = 16
# We'll construct protobuf wire format manually using these conventional tags.
# This yields bytes that ParseFromString for the same .proto definition will accept.

# Protobuf varint encoding helpers

def _encode_varint(value: int) -> bytes:
    """Encode a non-negative integer as protobuf varint."""
    if value < 0:
        # For int32 negative values, protobuf uses two's complement in varint.
        # But we only generate non-negative values here.
        value &= (1 << 64) - 1
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        to_write = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value:
            out.append(to_write | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(to_write)
            break
    return bytes(out)


def _encode_length_delimited(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _encode_varint(len(data)) + data


def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use a range of printable ASCII including spaces and punctuation to probe replace/split behaviors elsewhere
    alphabet = (
        "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789" \
        " -._/:@[](),;!$&'*=+?%\"\\\n\t"
    )
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _build_socket_endpoint(name: str | None, port: int | None) -> bytes:
    # Tags: name = field 1, wire type 2 (length-delimited) => 0x0A
    #       port = field 2, wire type 0 (varint)            => 0x10
    out = bytearray()
    if name is not None:
        name_bytes = name.encode('utf-8')
        out.append(0x0A)
        out += _encode_length_delimited(name_bytes)
    if port is not None:
        out.append(0x10)
        # int32 is varint; keep within 0..65535 as in stub
        if port < 0:
            port = 0
        if port > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            port &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        out += _encode_varint(port)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide presence of fields to exercise combinations similar to the fuzzer flags
    # 0: neither (empty message), 1: name only, 2: port only, 3: both
    mode = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3])  # bias toward both fields

    name: str | None = None
    port: int | None = None

    if mode & 1:
        # Choose varied lengths to hit small/medium/edge cases
        name_len_choice = rng.random()
        if name_len_choice < 0.2:
            name = ""  # empty string
        elif name_len_choice < 0.6:
            name = _random_ascii(rng, 1, 8)
        elif name_len_choice < 0.9:
            name = _random_ascii(rng, 9, 64)
        else:
            # longer but keep total under 4096 bytes
            name = _random_ascii(rng, 128, 1024)

    if mode & 2:
        # Generate ports across interesting values
        ports: List[int] = [0, 1, 22, 80, 443, 1024, 2048, 65535]
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            port = rng.choice(ports)
        else:
            port = rng.randint(0, 65535)

    msg = _build_socket_endpoint(name, port)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(msg) > 4096:
        # If too large due to name length, truncate name thoughtfully and rebuild
        if name is not None:
            # Keep encoded length within limit
            max_name_len = max(0, 4000)  # safe cap
            name = name[:max_name_len]
            msg = _build_socket_endpoint(name, port)
        # As a last resort, fall back to minimal message
        if len(msg) > 4096:
            msg = _build_socket_endpoint("", port if port is not None else 0)

    return msg

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: et::Packet wire format
# Bytes: [0]=encrypted flag (0/1), [1]=header (uint8), [2:]=payload (arbitrary)
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for payload and serialized. Our generator
# should return a bytes object that is an interesting serialized Packet buffer.

_ALNUM = b"0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce arbitrary but printable-biased bytes; include some non-printables too
    # to exercise binary payloads.
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            out.append(_ALNUM[rng.randrange(len(_ALNUM))])
        elif t < 0.9:
            out.append(rng.randrange(32, 127))  # common printable ASCII
        else:
            out.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))   # full byte range
    return bytes(out)


def _make_serialized_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose variants to toggle behaviors in Packet:
    # - encrypted flag 0/1
    # - header values: 0, 1, 255, random
    # - payload sizes: 0, small, medium, near limit for our 4096 cap
    header_choices = [0, 1, 255, rng.randrange(0, 256)]
    header = header_choices[rng.randrange(len(header_choices))] & 0xFF

    enc = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0

    # Payload strategies
    strategies = [
        (0, b""),
        (1, b"A" * 1),
        (2, b"".join([b"",])),  # another empty path
        (3, None),  # random small
        (4, None),  # random medium
        (5, None),  # random large but within 4096 total
        (6, b"\x00\x00\x00"),  # embedded nulls
        (7, b"header:test;enc:%d" % enc),
        (8, b"\xff\x01\x02\x03"),
        (9, b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"),
    ]
    kind, preset = strategies[rng.randrange(len(strategies))]

    if preset is not None:
        payload = preset
    else:
        if kind == 3:
            length = rng.randrange(1, 16)
        elif kind == 4:
            length = rng.randrange(16, 256)
        else:  # kind == 5
            # Keep total length <= 4096. We have 2 header bytes already.
            length = rng.randrange(256, 4096 - 2)
        payload = _rand_bytes(rng, length)

    # Optionally simulate ciphertext-like payload when enc==1 by making it more random
    if enc == 1 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        payload = bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(len(payload)))

    # Build wire format
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(enc & 1)
    out.append(header)
    out.extend(payload)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Mix seed path with variant selection to provide diversity across calls
    variant = rng.randrange(0, 10)

    # 70% of the time produce a valid serialized packet to satisfy the Packet(serialized) ctor.
    # 30% of the time produce a plausible payload for the other ctors (used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR too).
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        buf = _make_serialized_packet(rng)
        # Ensure minimum size >= 2 as required by the deserializing constructor
        if len(buf) < 2:
            buf = buf + b"\x00\x00"
        # Cap total size defensively
        return buf[:4096]
    else:
        # Return a payload string used by Packet(header, payload) paths.
        # Include interesting edge cases and random content.
        choices: List[bytes] = [
            b"",  # empty payload
            b"\x00",  # single NUL
            b"\xff" * 8,
            b"payload",
            b"JSON:{\"k\":\"v\"}",
            b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04",
            _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(1, 512)),
        ]
        return choices[variant % len(choices)][:4096]
